comments.author: sharkweek
comments.story: The New York Times Calls for Marijuana Legalization
comments.why: Documentary arguing drugs are a public health issue, not criminal
comments.text: Two plugs I always make during any drug law discussion on HN: One - The Economist's 2009 article "Failed states and failed policies" - [LINK] (you might have to Google the title to get around a paywall) Two - The documentary, The House I Live In - [LINK] (trailer - [VIDEO] ) Both make such a fascinating case that drugs should have never been a crime and punishment issue, but rather one of public health. I highly recommend both for a read and a watch, and both will articulate the case far superior to anything I would be able to write here.

comments.text: If you haven't already seen The House I Live In, I recommend watching the documentary online. It will change the way you think about drugs and the United States' prison system. The movie doesn't focus specifically on technology, but it explores the by-any-means-necessary approach to law enforcement that helps facilitate things such as the Hemisphere Project mentioned in the story. comments.story: Militarized police overreach — a second excerpt from Radley Balko's book
comments.why: Documentary on how drug laws drove mass incarceration and policing
comments.text: Since drug war/prison system/militarized police keeps popping up on HN, I'd highly recommend anyone very interested in learning more about how this came to be to watch the documentary "The House I Live In." Trailer: [VIDEO] Link to site: [LINK] It's an excellent explanation of how drug laws and being "tough" on crime have led to skyrocketing incarceration rates, trigger happy cops, and broken communities.
